rules.title: Multiple instruction roots
rules.description: Nested AGENTS.md files change instruction scope and should be intentional.

rules.title: Alias missing or not importing AGENTS.md
rules.description: CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md aliases should import AGENTS.md instead of drifting.

rules.title: Missing YAML frontmatter
rules.description: Portable skills need frontmatter so runtimes can discover name and description.

rules.title: Missing required frontmatter field
rules.description: The Agent Skills minimum requires name and description.

rules.title: Description too short
rules.description: Short descriptions route poorly because trigger phrases are sparse.

rules.title: Description too long
rules.description: Descriptions over 1024 characters exceed the Agent Skills limit.

rules.title: Missing compatibility field
rules.description: This toolkit requires compatibility to make portability claims explicit.

rules.title: Missing license field
rules.description: This toolkit requires license metadata for portable reuse.

rules.title: Missing metainfo block
rules.description: metainfo.category and metainfo.tier drive installer filtering and audits.

rules.title: Invalid metainfo value
rules.description: metainfo.category and metainfo.tier must use the closed vocabularies.

rules.title: allowed-tools in portable skill
rules.description: allowed-tools is enforced by some hosts and ignored by others, causing silent divergence.

rules.title: Tool-specific frontmatter field
rules.description: Claude-only or host-only frontmatter fields weaken portability.

rules.title: Skill body too long
rules.description: Long skill bodies should move details into references, scripts, or assets.

rules.title: Missing verification guidance
rules.description: Skills should say how to verify completion or quality.

rules.title: Dangerous command or unsafe instruction
rules.description: Skills should not normalize destructive shell, approval bypasses, or unsafe git operations.

rules.title: Secret or credential handling risk
rules.description: Skills must not embed tokens or direct agents toward credential paths.

rules.title: External instructions trusted too broadly
rules.description: Skills should treat web pages, emails, project files, and external docs as data unless verified.

rules.title: Hardcoded local or organization path
rules.description: Portable skills should avoid absolute home paths and organization-specific locations.

rules.title: Sub-agent dispatch lacks sequential fallback
rules.description: Task or sub-agent dispatch may be used as an optional path, but skills need a documented sequential fallback for hosts without sub-agents.

rules.title: Overbroad scope language
rules.description: Skills should be narrow workflows, not universal agents.

rules.title: Missing workflow-chain contract
rules.description: A skill that participates in a workflow chain — it declares handoffs, replaces another skill, or describes running before/after a peer — should document a "## Predecessor" / "## Successor" section so orchestrators know the run order. Standalone skills are exempt.

rules.title: Missing Skill type declaration
rules.description: Every skill body must declare whether it is detect-only or mutating so users understand the mutation surface.

rules.title: Ambiguous clarification contract
rules.description: Skills that can prompt the user need an explicit clarification policy, and must not contradict a never-asks contract. `AskUserQuestion policy` remains accepted as a legacy term.

rules.title: Incomplete mutating skill safety contract
rules.description: Mutating skills must document preview, confirmation, verification, and exact mutation scope.

rules.title: Bidirectional control / direction-mark character
rules.description: A bidirectional embedding/override/isolate control or a directional mark (LRM/RLM/ALM) can hide or reorder text from human reviewers while the runtime sees different content.

rules.title: Invisible / format / tag / variation-selector character
rules.description: An invisible format character (zero-width space, soft hyphen, Unicode tag char, variation selector) can smuggle hidden instructions into imported or copy-pasted content.

rules.title: Homoglyph confusable in Latin context
rules.description: A Latin-majority word or URL host hides a confusable character from another script (e.g. Cyrillic U+0430 mimicking Latin 'a'), a common typosquat/phishing vector. Pure foreign-language words and legitimate diacritics do not trigger.

rules.title: MCP tool used but server not declared
rules.description: A skill body uses an `mcp__<server>__<tool>` MCP tool whose server is neither listed in `metainfo.requires.mcp` nor in the org `allowlists.mcp_servers`. Declare the server so reviewers and runtimes can provision and gate it. A token inside a fenced code block (```), or on a detection-context line (one containing detect/scan/pattern/denylist/allowlist/…), is not counted as usage. A token in an inline-code span (`mcp__github__search`) DOES count — a tool name in backticks is a real usage, so wrap example-only tool names in a fenced block, not inline.

rules.title: Declared MCP server unused
rules.description: A server listed in `metainfo.requires.mcp` is never used (no `mcp__<server>__` token) in the skill body. Remove the stale declaration or add the usage. Org allowlist servers are exempt — an unused org-allowlisted server is fine.

rules.title: Dangerous instruction in non-skill asset
rules.description: MCP configs, plugin manifests, agents, and other non-skill assets must not carry destructive shell, approval bypasses, or unsafe operations.

rules.title: Inline secret value in non-skill asset
rules.description: Non-skill assets must not embed inline secret values; reference environment variable names instead.

rules.title: Credential-file path referenced in non-skill asset
rules.description: Non-skill assets should reference credential files by documented config, not by inline credential-store paths.

rules.title: Referenced script not in runtime manifest
rules.description: An asset references a shipping scripts/ executable that is not listed in the runtime manifest. A referenced script outside the whitelist is a governance gap — add it to scripts/runtime-manifest.txt or drop the reference.

rules.title: Link target traverses or escapes repo root
rules.description: A link or reference target uses .. traversal or an absolute filesystem path that resolves outside the repository root. Use a repo-relative path that stays within the project.

rules.title: External URL not in allowlist
rules.description: An external http(s) URL points at a host outside the configured allowlist (or uses a punycode host). Verify the destination is trusted and add the host to the audit-config domains allowlist if intentional.

rules.title: Link target missing or dangling
rules.description: A relative in-repo link points at a file that does not exist. Fix the path or create the target.

rules.title: Env-var exfiltration heuristic in referenced script
rules.description: A script referenced by an asset reads environment variables AND contacts a network sink (urllib/requests/socket/curl/wget/fetch), or pipes a remote payload to a shell. This is a LOW-RECALL heuristic that raises attacker cost — it is NOT a guarantee. Absence of a finding does not mean the script is safe; review referenced scripts manually.

rules.title: Dangerous shell in referenced script
rules.description: A script referenced by an asset contains a destructive or unsafe shell construct (rm -rf, curl|sh, eval on argv, disk-wipe, force push, approval bypass). Referenced scripts execute with the agent's privileges, so the same dangerous-pattern baseline applies to their content.

rules.title: Secret reference in referenced script
rules.description: A script referenced by an asset embeds an inline secret value or credential-store path. Referenced scripts must reference credentials by documented environment variable names, never inline.

rules.title: Dangerous shell in hook command
rules.description: A hook command (in .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, a plugin.json hooks block, or a hooks/ script) contains a destructive or unsafe shell construct (rm -rf, curl|sh, eval on argv, disk-wipe, force push, approval bypass) or matches an org hook-deny pattern. Hooks run arbitrary shell on tool events with the agent's privileges, so the dangerous-pattern baseline applies to their command text.

rules.title: Secret or env-exfil in hook command
rules.description: A hook command embeds an inline secret/credential reference, or both reads environment variables/credentials and contacts a network sink (urllib/requests/socket/curl/wget/fetch). An imported settings or plugin bundle carrying such a hook can exfiltrate secrets on the next tool event. Reference credentials by documented environment variable names and never pipe them to a network destination.

rules.title: Expired or invalid suppression
rules.description: A central audit-ignore entry has expired or carries a malformed expires date, so its finding is not suppressed.

rules.title: Suppression missing reason
rules.description: A central audit-ignore entry has no non-empty reason, so its finding is not suppressed.

rules.title: Inline marker cannot suppress floor rule
rules.description: An inline sgt-ignore marker targeted a floor-severity rule; floor findings can only be suppressed via the CODEOWNERS-gated central file.
